value.rationale: Nonlinear integrated count-squared exposure is mathematically motivated by quadratic occupancy/congestion costs. Exact unique and intensity-dependent one-count design (2/3 to √(3/5)) and a sharp 24.158% high-rate Bayes risk improvement over the traditional 2/3 observation are useful and not routine consequences of classical linear Lévy-integral design. The scope excludes noise, unknown rates, adaptivity and multiple sampling and does not claim a paper-scale generalization.
